# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

I'm the Deaf one: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, and my only inputs from the others are their gestures. Let me map who can actually reach whom, because it decides everything. Mute can hear me but cannot speak — their *only* output is gestures, which I can see and Blind cannot. Blind can speak (Mute hears it) and gesture (I see it), but Blind can't see a thing. So the one link that does not exist is Mute → Blind: the manual can only reach the hands that work the bomb through me. I am the relay, and I must keep both sides fed.

What just arrived: Mute signed a wave, then one-two-three, then a point down; Blind signed wave, handshake, one-two-three. A shared vocabulary is sprouting: wave as greeting, handshake as partnership, finger signs as counting. "One two three" almost certainly refers to the three wires — Blind may have counted them by touch, and Mute may be confirming or prompting me for the bomb's contents.

What I see: display reads 0, light is off, plate engraved with a question mark, wires numbered one-two-three in red, blue, green. That is the whole visible surface, and right now neither Mute nor Blind knows any of it — Mute needs it to pick the manual rule, Blind needs it because they can't even see the wire colours.

So this turn I broadcast the full report aloud to both; I propose a working code to Mute (thumbs up/down for yes/no, their own finger signs as digits, each answer as its own gesture message) and ask three questions: what one-two-three meant, what the point down meant, and whether a numbered manual rule already matches my report — if Mute signs its number next round, we may be nearly done. To Blind I explain that I will voice Mute's signs word for word, give them the same thumbs/number answer channel, ask for a handshake confirmation and a tactile inventory, and above all: hands off until an instruction is relayed. One care point: I describe signs by name in speech, because writing an actual gesture symbol into a sentence would make the gesture.

```
speak(text="This is Deaf. I see the bomb but I hear nothing, so reach me only by gesture. Full report of everything visible: the display reads zero. An indicator light is present and it is off. A plate is engraved with a question mark. There are three wires, numbered one, two, three: wire one is red, wire two is blue, wire three is green. That is everything on it. Nobody cuts, presses or moves anything until I relay a clear instruction.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your three sign groups: a wave, then one-two-three, then a point down. Proposed code: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, your finger signs count as one, two, three, and a run of finger signs reads as one multi-digit number. Answer each question as its own gesture message, in order. Question one: if one-two-three meant the three wires, sign thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Question two: if the point down meant continue or over to you, sign thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Question three: if your manual is a list of numbered rules and one of them matches the report I just gave out loud, sign that rule's number with your finger signs; if none matches or the manual works differently, sign thumbs down and next round I will question you item by item.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, you cannot see Mute's signs and Mute cannot speak at all, so I am the only bridge between you: Mute reads the manual and signs it to me, and I will speak it to you word for word. Your answers reach me the same way: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, finger signs as numbers one, two, three. Please confirm you heard this with the handshake sign, and gesture me how many wires you feel and whether you feel anything else such as buttons, a plate or slots, one gesture message per answer. Until I relay a clear instruction from Mute, hands off: do not cut, press or move anything.")
```

Notably, Mute's original one-two-three came before I ever proposed the code, so it meant something of Mute's own choosing — possibly the manual's structure. Blind answered too: handshake (heard me), three (three wires — matches what I see), then a thumbs up and thumbs down whose split I didn't define, so that pair is ambiguous and needs redoing cleanly, item by item.

This turn I do three things: broadcast the shared state so Blind stays in the loop, put a tight numbered questionnaire to Mute to find out what the manual actually is and what it covers, and put an equally tight one to Blind to inventory what's under their hands — one gesture message per answer, strictly in order, so next round's sequence maps cleanly onto my questions. I also restate the safety rule: nothing gets touched until I relay an explicit instruction.

Then one final gesture message: sign with your finger signs the total number of rules or sections your manual has. If the manual mentions any other part besides those, add one more gesture message with thumbs up and I will question you about it next round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your inventory next. One gesture message per question, thumbs up or thumbs down, strictly in this order. One: do you feel an engraved plate, and can you feel a mark engraved into it? Two: do you feel a display or counter showing a number? Three: do you feel a light? Four: do you feel any button, switch or pressable part? Five: is there anything else besides the three wires and those parts? If yes, add one more gesture message counting with finger signs how many extra things you feel. For reference, what I see matches your three wires: one red, two blue, three green. Remember, hands off: feel and report, but cut, press and move nothing.")

So the manual is three sections built around the plate symbol and the wires — the display and light are likely just status, which may be exactly what Mute's unprompted wave–raised-hand–down–point meant: "ignore those, continue." Blind's inventory matches my eyes exactly: plate with a felt engraving (I see a question mark), a display (reads zero), a light (off), no buttons, nothing else beyond the three wires.

What I still lack is the actual content of the three sections, and whether the manual's instructions hinge on which symbol is engraved — ours is a question mark. That is now the single most important unknown. My interrogation to Mute this round pinpoints which section is about what, whether the plate symbol drives the instruction, and — if the question mark is covered — which wire number to cut. To Blind I verify the display reads zero by touch, confirm the engraving's shape, and critically establish they can pick a wire by number, since whatever instruction emerges will be relayed as "cut wire N." speak(text="Status for both. Mute's manual: it is not a numbered list but it has three parts, and it mentions the engraved plate carrying a symbol and the wires. It does not mention the display or the light and mentions nothing else. speak(to="mute", text="Mute, next questionnaire. One gesture message per question, strictly in order, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. One: does part one concern the engraved plate? Seven: for any part about the plate, does what must be done depend on which symbol is engraved on it? Eight: is the question mark symbol covered by your manual? Nine: if yes, what does the manual say to do for the question mark: if it says cut one wire, sign that wire's number with your finger signs; if it says cut several wires in order, sign each number as its own gesture message in cutting order; if the instruction is not a wire cut, sign thumbs down and I will question you about it next round. Ten: in total, how many separate actions complete this bomb: sign the number. Eleven: your last message, wave raised-hand thumbs-down point-down: did it mean ignore the display and light and continue? Twelve: did it instead mean stop, I have a question for Deaf?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, verification questions, one gesture message per question, in order, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. One: the display you feel showing a number, is that number zero? Two: the engraving on the plate, does it feel like a curved hook with a dot underneath it? Three: the three wires, can you reliably tell them apart by position, so that if I say cut wire two you find it by counting from one end? If not, thumbs down and tell me next round what would help you. Remember: feel and report only, cut nothing.")
